status: Version 4 (8:35 AM ET): adds the perceptual (LPIPS-vgg) and FLUX.2-latent objectives, a temporal objective for fast clips, two more fine-tuned encoders (ft2, video-only ft3) and position-balanced blind A/B tests. The remaining objectives, a longer 'ceiling' optimization and the rest of the images are still running.
verdict: By the numbers yes, by eye only partly. Latents exist that the frozen decoder turns into clearly better reconstructions on every reference metric: +4.1 dB PSNR on images and +2.5 dB on 5 whole clips, DISTS down by 60%. They stay as close to the encoder's latent as the pipeline's own sampling noise. A perceptual objective (LPIPS-vgg) makes decodes measurably sharper than the encoder's (gradient energy 0.96 → 0.98 of the source, DISTS 0.061 → 0.019), and a blind judge prefers both optimized versions in about two thirds of zoomed crops. What improves is color, contrast, edges and texture, not fine detail that was lost: hair strands, frets and rooftops stay soft, and on fast clips every decode keeps less frame-to-frame detail than the source. That part is the decoder's limit. A trained encoder (decoder frozen) captures only a part: the best one gains +1.0 dB on 20 held-out clips (+0.5 dB over H3's own tiled encode) and +2.6 dB on images, better on all six metrics for 18 of 20 clips, but a blind judge does not see it. Pixel-perfect video is not in reach with this decoder.
numbers: 12 held-out images (8 Pexels frames, 4 MAGICK on gray, 512²), latent optimized with L1 + 0.1·LPIPS-vgg for 100 Adam steps: PSNR 31.12 → 35.22 dB (every image gains, +2.0 to +6.1 dB); held-out judges (no objective used them): DISTS 0.061 → 0.024, FLUX.2 latent MSE 0.329 → 0.205, LPIPS-alex 0.055 → 0.040; all 12 better on all six of PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS-alex, DISTS, FLUX.2 MSE, CIEDE2000.

5 whole 141-frame clips, 60 Adam steps through all 8 decoder chunks: PSNR 31.02 → 33.50 dB (+1.6 to +3.0 each), LPIPS-alex 0.068 → 0.048, DISTS 0.056 → 0.026; all 5 better on all six metrics. Flicker: unchanged or lower on the 3 calm clips (0.142 → 0.142, 0.58 → 0.50, 0.31 → 0.28), higher on the 2 fast ones (park 1.90 → 2.45, cliffs 1.48 → 2.28): the per-frame objective does not watch motion; a run with a temporal term is running.

Objective matters. Plain L2: +5.1 dB PSNR, but DISTS worse than the encoder (0.068 vs 0.061): blur. LPIPS-vgg alone: +1.0 dB PSNR, DISTS 0.061 → 0.019, LPIPS-alex 0.055 → 0.040, sharpness 0.957 → 0.982 (gradient) and 0.870 → 0.911 (high frequencies): the sharpest. FIBO2's FLUX.2-latent distance alone (4 MAGICK images so far): FLUX MSE 0.26 → 0.09, DISTS 0.047 → 0.031, PSNR unchanged.

Blind A/B, position-balanced (each zoomed crop shown twice, sides swapped; fresh Sonnet judge; the judges favor the right-hand panel 60–77% of the time, which this design cancels): L1 + LPIPS latent preferred in 31 of 48 (11 crops both ways vs 4 for the encoder), LPIPS latent in 32 of 48 (9 vs 1), the fine-tuned encoder ft2 in only 21 of 48 on Pexels photos (2 vs 5). My own look agrees: truer skin and object colors, crisper frets and lugs, no chroma halos on graphics; hair and rooftops about as soft.
Pure PSNR is the wrong objective: plain L2 reaches +5.1 dB but makes DISTS worse than the encoder (0.068 vs 0.061): blur. L1 + LPIPS improves every metric.

The optimized latents move by RMS 0.077 (images) and 0.063 (clips) from the posterior mode; the pipeline's own posterior sample moves by 0.060 / 0.039. Per-channel means shift by 0.017 on average and per-channel spreads stay within 0.985–1.043 of the encoder's.
A free win: a tiled encode with H3's own encoder already improves clips (LPIPS 0.055 → 0.046, DISTS 0.056 → 0.047, flicker 0.43 → 0.42, +0.45 dB); the project encodes untiled for speed.

Fine-tuned encoders (H3's encoder + quant_conv, 180 M parameters, retrained with the decoder frozen; L1 + 0.1·LPIPS-vgg plus a penalty on (z − zH3)²). Tiled or untiled? All were trained on 256² crops, so every training input was exactly one 256-px tile (the tiled regime), with the penalty computed on the same crops; they are scored on full 512² frames both untiled and tiled. ft1 (1,000 steps, images + video, penalty 1.0), tiled: images 32.53 → 34.86 dB, clips 33.91 → 34.73 dB; untiled only +1.9 / +0.3 dB. ft2 (1,500 steps, 5× the learning rate, penalty 0.1), tiled: images +2.6 dB (47 of 49 better on all six), clips +0.8 dB. ft3 (700 steps, video windows only), tiled: 20 clips 33.64 → 34.64 dB, LPIPS 0.057 → 0.045, DISTS 0.056 → 0.042, 18 of 20 better on all six; against H3's own tiled encode (34.12 dB) that is +0.5 dB. Every fine-tune lowers the frame-to-frame detail a little more (flicker score 0.47 → 0.66) and the high-frequency energy (0.88 → 0.85).

Fast clips: a loss on frame-to-frame differences (l1_vgg_t) did not help: park clip temporal change source 12.9, encoder 11.1, optimized 10.5 (L1 + LPIPS) and 10.5 (with the temporal term). The decoder cannot produce that temporal texture (grain, fast fine motion) from any latent we found.
method:
1. Samples (held out, never trained on): the 20 held-out Pexels clips of the decoder frenzy (the clips BASELINE.json scores), as whole 141-frame clips and as their frame 70 (512²), plus 8 MAGICK foregrounds over 50% gray and their Pexels backgrounds at 512² and 768².
  2. Encoder baselines: the same untiled encode as the project. Posterior sample is the latent the pipeline trains on (seeded); mode drops that noise; tiled encodes in overlapping 256² tiles.
  3. Latent optimization: Adam on the whole latent, starting at the posterior mode, learning rate 0.01 with a cosine decay to 0.001, 100 steps for images (60 for clips). The decoder is frozen and runs exactly as the pipeline decodes: bf16, 256-pixel tiles, one image decoded as its latent repeated 7 times (frame 0 kept), a clip's 8 temporal chunks together. Gradient checkpointing per decoder block; for clips the loss is taken frame batch by frame batch on a detached copy of the decode, then one backward through the decoder. Cost on one A100: about 2 s per image per step, 22 s per clip per step.
  4. Objectives: l2, l1 (pixels), lpips_vgg, lpips_alex, flux (MSE between FLUX.2-VAE latents of the decode and of the source; FIBO2's image encoder), l1_vgg = L1 + 0.1·LPIPS-vgg, l1_vgg_flux = l1_vgg + 0.01·flux, and l1_vgg with a prior that keeps the latent inside the encoder's spread.
  5. Judges: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS (alex and vgg), DISTS (no objective uses it), FLUX.2 latent MSE, CIEDE2000, sharpness ratios, flicker (clips), all vs the source; then zoomed crops viewed by eye and a blind A/B by a fresh model agent.
  6. Fine-tuned encoder: a copy of H3's encoder trained with the decoder frozen on Bluejay train data (train Pexels clips and MAGICK images, never a held-out clip), 256² crops (one decoder tile), 34-frame windows (two encoder chunks, decoded as one 22-frame decoder chunk) plus single frames, loss L1 + 0.1·LPIPS-vgg plus a penalty on (z − zH3)² to stay in the latent distribution H3's diffusion model knows; then the same held-out scoring.
finding: The project encodes untiled (3× faster). That gives latents whose spread in channels 16–23 is only about 0.7 of what H3's own normalization expects, in the 300 stored training latents as in fresh re-encodes. The spread depends on the size of the picture the encoder sees: 128-px tiles give 1.39, the VAE's default 256-px tiles 0.96, 384-px tiles 0.76, the whole 512² frame 0.67. Only the default tiles match H3. Stock H3 agrees: its flow-matching loss on the same 30 clips is lower for tiled latents at every noise level, on 29–30 of 30 clips, about 10% lower on average. So H3 was trained on latents like the tiled ones, and every adapter of this project so far was trained on latents slightly off H3's distribution. The tiled encode also decodes better (on 18 held-out clips LPIPS 0.055 → 0.046, DISTS 0.056 → 0.047).
